title: Does Evaluation-Awareness Actually Change Control Behavior? A Narrow Replication

original_idea.body: On a small sabotage task run an open model under matched prompts differing only in evaluation-salience cues and measure whether sabotage rate and CoT verbalization change, reporting effect sizes.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Isolating eval-awareness behavioral effect in sabotage settings governs the external validity of control evals.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Matched-prompt sabotage task with salience cues, measure effect sizes; accessible, prompt-only.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Prompt-only, public models, resolves a live disagreement, lab-independent.

novelty.reasoning: Eval-awareness heavily studied in 2026; the control/sabotage-specific isolation may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Eval-awareness studied broadly; sabotage-setting isolation may be open.
